previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, chronic hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease, was admitted for evaluation of bloody diarrhea. He reported over 10 episodes of bright red, loose stools without fever, vomiting, or recent travel. Initial labs showed anemia with hemoglobin of 7.3 g/dL, prompting a red blood cell transfusion. A CT abdomen and pelvis showed no colitis, diverticulitis, or other structural cause. Stool studies were inconclusive, with C. diff testing cancelled due to soft stool and norovirus negative. The diarrhea resolved spontaneously, and he remained hemodynamically stable. His hemoglobin stabilized at 8.5 g/dL post-transfusion. Chemotherapy with carfilzomib was held during the acute episode but planned for resumption post-discharge. Blood pressure and diabetes medications were adjusted during admission and resumed at discharge. He was discharged home with services, instructions to use loperamide as needed, and follow-up plans with oncology and primary care.
